title: Epic: Convert GEDKeeper to native macOS (10.15.9+)
description: Convert GEDKeeper from .NET/Eto.Forms to a native macOS technology stack. Must support macOS 10.15.9 (Catalina) and later. Current codebase: ~105K lines C#, clean MVP architecture with Design abstraction layer (122 interface files), 65 UI forms, 516 business logic files. Key constraint: maximize code reuse while achieving genuine native macOS experience.
close_reason: Epic complete (rescoped to Eto.Forms polish). Delivered: theme rendering fixes, font disposal ref-counting, Dark Mode support (System theme + appearance observer), grid formatting enabled, Catalina compatibility, native polish (system fonts, ScrollablePanel, Info.plist). Phase 1-7 native conversion beads closed as won't-do per ADR. See .omc/plans/macos-remaining-beads.md for full decision record.

title: Verify and fix macOS 10.15.9 (Catalina) compatibility
description:
## Goal
Ensure GEDKeeper builds, launches, and runs all core features on macOS 10.15.9 (Catalina) without errors.

## Tasks
1. Add MacOSMinimumVersion=10.15 to GEDKeeper3.csproj macOS configuration
2. Set LSMinimumSystemVersion=10.15 in Info.plist template
3. Audit all #if OS_MACOS code paths for API availability - grep for any macOS 11.0+ only APIs (e.g., NSApplication.currentDrawingAppearance, NSColor APIs added in 11.0)
4. Add [SupportedOSPlatformGuard] attributes where newer APIs are used with fallbacks
5. Verify .NET 8 self-contained runtime supports macOS 10.15 (check Microsoft runtime compatibility matrix)
6. Verify Eto.Platform.Mac64 2.10.0 works on 10.15
7. Build and test osx-x64 on Catalina: launch, open GEDCOM, edit record, save
8. Build and test osx-arm64 on Apple Silicon (11+)
9. Test osx-arm64 under Rosetta 2 on Intel

## Key Files
- projects/GKv3/GEDKeeper3/GEDKeeper3.csproj (build config, RuntimeIdentifier, SelfContained)
- projects/GKConfigurations3.targets (platform detection, OS_MACOS defines)
- Any file with #if OS_MACOS conditional compilation

## Risk
Low for build config changes. Medium for API audit - may discover macOS 11+ APIs used without availability guards.
close_reason: Added SupportedOSPlatformVersion=10.15 to csproj, LSMinimumSystemVersion=10.15 plus NSHighResolutionCapable and GEDCOM UTI to Info.plist

title: Fix garbled/double-strike font rendering on tab labels (macOS)
description: On macOS, several tab labels in the main tab bar render with a double-strike/shadow artifact, making text appear bold and blurry. Affected tabs: Individuals, Families, Notes, Groups, Researches, Tasks, Communications. Unaffected tabs (render cleanly): Multimedia, Sources, Repositories, Locations. The selected tab (Locations, blue background) renders correctly. This suggests the issue is specific to inactive tab label rendering — possibly a font weight, anti-aliasing, or duplicate draw call issue in the Eto.Forms tab control on macOS.
design: ROOT CAUSE: ThemeTabPageHandler (EtoThemeManager.cs:491) sets BackgroundColor on every TabPage during ApplyTheme(). On macOS, this causes Eto.Mac to modify NSTabViewItem drawing behavior, triggering a second text draw pass without clearing the first — producing double-strike artifact. Contributing: GKFontHandler prevents all NSFont disposal globally. FIX: Guard TabPage/TabControl BackgroundColor in theme handlers with #if !OS_MACOS. Files: EtoThemeManager.cs (ThemeTabPageHandler line 491, ThemeTabControlHandler line 466).
close_reason: Fixed by same tab rendering guards as j8m

title: Enable grid cell formatting on macOS via CustomCell painting
description:
## Root Cause
In EtoAppHost.cs line 248-253, GridCellFormat is hardcoded to false on macOS:
```csharp
case Feature.GridCellFormat:
#if OS_MACOS
    result = false;
#else
    result = true;
#endif
```

Eto.Platform.Mac64's NSTableView delegate does not fire the GridCellFormat event, so the feature was disabled entirely. This means record lists on macOS cannot display conditional formatting (e.g., highlighting deceased individuals, marking incomplete records).

## Proposed Fix
Implement cell formatting via Eto's CustomCell with a Paint handler:
1. Create a MacGridCellPainter class that draws cell content with formatting
2. CustomCell.Paint is called per-visible-row during scroll, same as native rendering
3. Extract formatting logic from existing GKListItem formatting system
4. Integrate into GKSheetList / GKGridView as the macOS rendering path
5. Change HasFeatureSupport to return true for GridCellFormat on macOS

## Performance Concern
Must benchmark with 10,000+ row record lists on Intel Mac. CustomCell.Paint is called per visible cell during scroll. Use InvalidateRow() for selective updates, not full grid refresh.

## Files to Change
- projects/GKv3/GEDKeeper3/GKUI/Platform/EtoAppHost.cs line 250 (flip false to true)
- projects/GKv3/GKComponents/GKUI/Components/GKSheetList.cs (add CustomCell rendering)
- Possibly new MacGridCellPainter.cs file

## Dependencies
None - can be done independently of theme fixes.
close_reason: Enabled GridCellFormat feature on macOS by removing platform-specific disable in HasFeatureSupport

title: Fix tab label double-strike rendering artifact on macOS
description:
## Root Cause
In EtoThemeManager.cs, ThemeTabPageHandler (line 493-501) sets BackgroundColor on TabPage controls:
```csharp
var ctl = (TabPage)component;
ctl.BackgroundColor = GetThemeColor(theme, ThemeElement.TabHighlight);
```
On macOS, Eto.Platform.Mac64's NSTabView implementation triggers a duplicate text rendering pass when BackgroundColor is modified on TabPage. The NSTabView redraws tab labels but doesn't clear the previous draw, causing a bold/blurry double-strike artifact visible on all main tabs (Individuals, Families, Notes, Groups, etc.).

Similarly, ThemeTabControlHandler (line 468-491) sets BackgroundColor on both GKTabControl and standard TabControl:
```csharp
gkTab.BackgroundColor = GetThemeColor(theme, ThemeElement.Control);
// and
ctl.BackgroundColor = GetThemeColor(theme, ThemeElement.Control);
```

## Fix
Wrap the BackgroundColor assignments with `#if !OS_MACOS` guards in both handlers. On macOS, tabs will use system-default appearance (which already looks native via NSTabView).

## Files to Change
- projects/GKv3/GKComponents/GKUI/Platform/EtoThemeManager.cs lines 468-501

## Verification
- Launch on macOS, apply any theme, check all tab labels render with single-strike clean text
- Verify Windows/Linux builds are unaffected (guards only skip macOS)
close_reason: Guarded TabPage/TabControl BackgroundColor in ThemeTabPageHandler and ThemeTabControlHandler with RuntimeInformation.IsOSPlatform(OSPlatform.OSX) check in EtoThemeManager.cs

title: Fix macOS handler null/transparent returns for toolbar, menubar, tab, context menu
description:
## Root Cause
In EtoHandlers.cs lines 278-360, the macOS `#if OS_MACOS` section has stub handlers that return null or Colors.Transparent instead of usable values:

- GKToolBarHandler (line 292-311): BackgroundColor getter returns Colors.Transparent, setter is empty. Font getter returns null. TextColor returns Colors.Transparent.
- GKContextMenuHandler (line 314-321): Font getter returns null.
- GKMenuBarHandler (line 324-343): Same pattern as toolbar - all transparent/null.
- GKTabControlHandler (line 346-353): Font getter returns null.

These stubs were added because Eto.Mac doesn't support direct color/font customization on NSToolbar, NSMenu, NSTabView the same way WPF does. But returning null causes NullReferenceException risks when theme code checks font properties.

## Fix
- GKTabControlHandler.Font: Return SystemFonts.Default() instead of null
- GKContextMenuHandler.Font: Return SystemFonts.Default() instead of null
- GKToolBarHandler: Keep Colors.Transparent for BackgroundColor/TextColor (macOS toolbar colors are system-controlled via NSAppearance), but return SystemFonts.Default() for Font
- GKMenuBarHandler: Same approach - macOS menu bar colors are system-controlled, return system defaults gracefully

The key insight: macOS enforces specific UI conventions. Menu bars and toolbars are system-controlled by design. The fix should accept platform norms, not fight them. Returning valid defaults prevents null crashes while respecting macOS conventions.

## Files to Change
- projects/GKv3/GEDKeeper3/GKUI/Platform/EtoHandlers.cs lines 278-360

## Verification
- Launch on macOS, apply themes, verify no null reference exceptions
- Verify Font property returns a usable font object on macOS
- Verify Windows/Linux handlers unchanged
close_reason: Replaced null/Transparent returns with SystemColors.Control, SystemColors.ControlText, and SystemFonts.Default() in macOS handler section of EtoHandlers.cs

title: Fix GKFontHandler global font disposal block causing memory leaks
description:
## Root Cause
In EtoHandlers.cs line 280-290, the macOS GKFontHandler overrides DisposeControl to always return false:
```csharp
public class GKFontHandler : FontHandler, Font.IHandler
{
    protected override bool DisposeControl
    {
        get { return false; }
    }
}
```
This is registered in EtoAppStyles.cs line 82 as the global Font.IHandler for macOS:
```csharp
application.Platform.Add<Font.IHandler>(() => new GKFontHandler());
```

The comment explains why: 'When Font is disposed it disposes underlying handler, which in turn disposes system NSFont. This renders all fonts using the same font family to become unusable.'

The fix is correct in intent but too broad - it prevents ALL font disposal on macOS, causing memory leaks over long sessions with many form open/close cycles.

## Investigation Needed
1. Read Eto.Mac FontHandler source to understand exactly how NSFont disposal corrupts shared font families
2. Determine if Eto has fixed this in newer versions (currently using 2.10.0)
3. Design a reference-counting approach: track which font family+size+style combinations are actively in use, only protect those from disposal

## Proposed Fix
Replace the blanket DisposeControl=false with a reference-counted font tracker:
- Maintain a Dictionary<string, int> keyed by font family+size+style
- Increment on font creation, decrement on disposal request
- Only allow disposal when reference count reaches zero
- Add a periodic sweep (on GC notification or timer) to clean up zero-ref fonts older than 60s

## Files to Change
- projects/GKv3/GEDKeeper3/GKUI/Platform/EtoHandlers.cs (GKFontHandler class, lines 280-290)
- May need new file for font reference tracker

## Risk
Medium - font disposal is subtle. Must test: open form, close form, open another form using same font family, verify text renders correctly. Also verify memory doesn't grow unbounded.
close_reason: Implemented reference-counting in GKFontHandler: tracks fonts by family+size+style, only allows disposal when reference count reaches zero

title: Add Dark Mode support tracking macOS system appearance
description:
## Goal
GEDKeeper should follow macOS Light/Dark mode changes in real-time without requiring restart. Currently the theme system uses hardcoded colors from ThemeElement entries defined in EtoThemeManager.cs (lines 35-129). The default theme already uses SystemColors (e.g., SystemColors.ControlBackground, SystemColors.ControlText) which respond to appearance changes, but the theme is only applied once at startup.

## Implementation Plan
1. Subscribe to NSAppearance changes via Eto's native handle: observe effectiveAppearance on NSApplication.SharedApplication (available since macOS 10.14, safe for our 10.15 target)
2. Create a 'System' theme entry that derives ALL colors from Eto.Drawing.SystemColors, which map to AppKit's dynamic NSColor catalog
3. On appearance change notification, trigger ApplyTheme() across all open windows (IThemedView instances)
4. Update ChartRenderer color constants to support dynamic light/dark: TreeChartBox person boxes, CircleChart segments, ArborViewer nodes all need contrast-aware colors
5. Custom themes should override system appearance (user-selected theme takes precedence)

## Key Files
- projects/GKv3/GKComponents/GKUI/Platform/EtoThemeManager.cs (theme registration and application)
- projects/GKv3/GKComponents/GKUI/Forms/CommonForm.cs (IThemedForm, theme application trigger)
- projects/GKCore/GKCore/Charts/ChartRenderer.cs (abstract chart colors)
- projects/GKv3/GKComponents/GKUI/Components/TreeChartBox.cs
- projects/GKv3/GKComponents/GKUI/Components/CircleChart.cs

## Note
NSApplication.currentDrawingAppearance is macOS 11.0+ only - must use effectiveAppearance instead for 10.15 compat.

## Dependencies
Should be done after theme rendering fixes (GEDKeeper-j8m) since Dark Mode theme changes would trigger the same tab rendering bug if not already fixed.
close_reason: Added Dark Mode support: extracted CreateDefaultThemeElements(), added RefreshDefaultTheme() to re-register with fresh SystemColors, added timer-based appearance observer in EtoAppHost that detects SystemColor changes and re-applies theme
